# M4 Status (in progress): Owen Pendleton, Bryan Rosas

## Hardware wired and checked on the Pi (2026-11-13)
Wired with the Pi powered off, using female-to-female jumpers (no breadboard).

| Part | Wire | Header pin | Signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| HC-SR501 PIR | brown, VCC | pin 2 | 5 V |
| | orange, GND | pin 6 | GND |
| | red, OUT | pin 11 | GPIO17 (pird's default `--line=17`) |
| Arm button module (`-`, middle, `S`) | yellow, S | pin 13 | GPIO27, Pi pull-up, **pressed = low** |
| | blue, - | pin 14 | GND |
| | middle pin | not connected | the Pi's internal pull-up replaces it |
| RTC cell | JST plug | J5 `BAT` | n/a |
| LED | not bought yet | pin 15 (GPIO22) kept free | n/a |

The PIR's knobs were left at factory settings (they're unlabelled on this
board). The RTC cell has no printed type, so trickle charging is **off**
(`rtc_bbat_vchg` not set). Enable it only after confirming an ML
(rechargeable) cell.

**Bring-up checks (stock tools, no project code):**
- PIR, `gpiomon GPIO17`: `rising` on a wave, `falling` a few seconds
  later, quiet for 20 s while still.
- Button, `gpiomon --bias=pull-up GPIO27`: `falling` on press, `rising`
  on release.
- RTC, `timedatectl`: RTC time 22:59 UTC matched local time (MST). With
  Wi-Fi and Ethernet disconnected, `sudo poweroff`, unplugged for 3 min,
  then booted: local time matched a phone, with `System clock
  synchronized: no`, so the time came from the RTC. (`hwclock` isn't
  installed on this image; use `timedatectl`.)

## PIR through the real pipeline (M3 code, before fusion)
`deploy/run-m3.sh` (PIR, camera; no mic), first real-PIR run of `pird`:
```
pird: start pid=1696 chip=/dev/gpiochip0 line=17 mode=irq level=0; warm-up, edges ignored until T+60s
16:18:44.719 pird: warm-up over, armed (line level=0)
16:19:14.931 pird: edge rise lat=22us
16:19:14.931 hub: event 4 opened (PIR rise)
16:19:14.934 camd: burst 4 started: 20 frames every 500 ms (rpicam-still pid 1704)
16:19:25.641 camd: burst 4 done: 18 frames
16:19:25.858 hub: event 4: committed 18 images to clips/4.dir
16:20:16.821 hub: event 4 closed: MOTION_ONLY dur=61.9s edges=9 images=18 audio-offline
```
- Edge-to-userspace latency (mechanism B, IRQ mode) was 17-33 us across
  both runs, with one 97 us edge during a camera burst.
- PIR pulses were ~0.45 s high, at least ~2.5 s apart while someone was
  in view. The event stayed open because the PIR kept re-firing, and it
  closed at Ctrl-C (`hub: exit 0`).
- `build/pss events` listed event 4.

## Fusion: camera only on a confirmed ENTRY (commit 44ff06a)
- **Rule** (`src/analysis/fusion.c`, called from the hub): a PIR rise
  and a sound onset within **T_co = 5 s** of each other, in either order,
  make an ENTRY. The ENTRY is made durable at once (EVENT_OPEN), and only
  then is the camera fired.
- **Motion alone or sound alone** is logged (MOTION_ONLY / SOUND_ONLY)
  with **no images**.
- T_co was changed from 3 s to 5 s at the team's request (DESIGN.md
  Section 4 updated); `--t-co-ms` overrides it.
- **Lab machine:** `make`, `make test`, `make asan`, `make memcheck` and
  `make netcheck` pass. The new `test_fusion` covers the window
  boundaries, both orders and out-of-order arrival. The new
  `test_entry_to_storage` covers sound->motion and motion->sound (ENTRY
  with images), too far apart (no images), and camera failure (ENTRY
  kept, flagged no-images).
- **On the Pi** (`deploy/run-m3.sh --mic --mic-device=plughw:CARD=Snowball`,
  PIR wired), results as observed by Bryan (no log captured):
  1. Motion only, silent: event closed MOTION_ONLY, images=0.
  2. Clap, sensor covered: no images. Labelled MOTION_ONLY because the
     PIR fired during the event, more than 5 s from the clap. An event's
     label is MOTION_ONLY whenever it saw any PIR edge and wasn't an
     ENTRY. The team decided that's acceptable, since only ENTRY drives
     the camera.
  3. Clap and motion together: ENTRY, images taken and saved.

## Arm button in pird (Owen, branch `m4-arm-button`)
- `pird` requests GPIO27 together with the PIR line (pull-up, both
  edges, kernel timestamps). A fall counts as a press only if the line
  was high for at least the debounce period before it
  (`src/capture/pir/button_logic.c`, tested by `tests/test_button_logic.c`).
  It is debounced by the kernel and in software in IRQ mode, and in
  software only with `--poll`. The PIR warm-up does not apply to it. Each
  press goes to the hub as `PSS_MSG_BUTTON`. The hub only logs it
  (`arm button press #N`, approved by Bryan); the arm state machine is
  still to come.
- **Lab machine:** `make`, `make test`, `make asan`, `make memcheck`,
  `make netcheck` pass. pird doesn't build there (no libgpiod v2).
- **Raw bounce on the Pi** (debounce off, `--button-debounce-ms=0`):
  - 10 presses gave 12 counted. The 2 extras were release bounces,
    12 µs and 38 µs after a release. Each bouncing release settled
    within 0.64 ms.
  - Presses never bounced.
  - `gpiomon`, 11 presses: one release bounced, for about 0.23 ms.
  - With debounce off the kernel once reported two falls in a row
    10 µs apart: edge direction is unreliable during a fast bounce. So
    the kernel debounce is kept on in IRQ mode, not only the software
    filter.
- **Chosen debounce: 20 ms** (the default). That is about 30x the
  longest bounce, and far below the gap between real presses (at least
  1 s here).
- **20-press checks** (`deploy/run-m3.sh`, PIR wired, no mic):

  | Mode | pird `press #` | hub `arm button press` | bounces | dropped |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | IRQ, kernel+software 20 ms | 20 | 20 | 0 | 0 |
  | `--poll=10`, software 20 ms | 20 | 20 | 0 | 0 |

  - Presses #1-13 of the IRQ run came during the PIR's 60 s warm-up and
    were all forwarded: no warm-up on the button.
  - IRQ latency was 7-33 µs.
  - With kernel debounce on, button timestamps fall on about a 4 ms grid.
    The kernel stamps the event when its debounce timer fires, so for
    the button `lat=` is measured from the end of the debounce, not from
    the contact. Press-to-hub delay is about 20-24 ms. Mechanism B
    latency numbers should therefore come from the PIR line, or from
    the button with debounce off.

## Arm state machine in the hub (Bryan, commit 32478e1)
- **Rule** (`src/analysis/arm.c`, called from the hub; DESIGN.md
  Section 4): DISARMED --button--> EXIT_DELAY (60 s) --> ARMED
  --ENTRY--> GRACE (30 s). A press in GRACE disarms and labels the entry
  `owner`. If GRACE runs out, the entry is labelled `reported`.
  `--exit-delay-ms` and `--grace-ms` override the times.
- **Decisions DESIGN.md left open** (Bryan, now in DESIGN.md Section 4):
  1. A press while ARMED (no entry yet, e.g. a quiet entry with no
     sound) disarms.
  2. A press during EXIT_DELAY cancels back to DISARMED, so a double
     press cancels arming.
  3. The state survives a restart or power cut. A restart during
     EXIT_DELAY starts the full delay over. A restart during GRACE comes
     back ARMED with the entry `reported`, so pulling the plug can't hide
     an entry.
  4. While DISARMED or in EXIT_DELAY, no new events are recorded and the
     camera never fires. An event already open when the device is
     disarmed finishes normally, so an `owner` entry keeps its images.
- **Storage:** every arm change is a new `PSS_REC_ARM` record in the
  events log, fsynced at once. The hub restores the last one at start.
  `pss events` prints these records, with the owner/reported label.
- **Hub:** button presses are accepted from pird only. The LED state is
  logged (`arm: LED blink/off (not wired yet)`) until it is wired.
- **Lab machine:** `make`, `make test`, `make asan`, `make memcheck` and
  `make netcheck` pass.
  - The new `test_arm` covers every transition and both timeouts at
    their exact boundaries.
  - The existing e2e tests now arm the hub first, since a fresh hub
    records nothing. Their checks are unchanged.
  - The new `test_arm_decisions` runs a real hub. It covers each decision
    above, including SIGKILL during GRACE and during EXIT_DELAY. Hub log
    from that run:
    ```
    hub: arm: EXIT_DELAY -> DISARMED (button)
    hub: arm: ARMED -> DISARMED (button)
    hub: arm: GRACE -> DISARMED (button), event 1 labelled owner
    hub: arm: GRACE -> ARMED (grace over), event 2 labelled reported
    hub: store: event 3 was open when power was lost; closed as interrupted (0 images kept)
    hub: arm: GRACE -> ARMED (restart), event 3 labelled reported
    hub: arm: EXIT_DELAY -> EXIT_DELAY (restart)
    ```
- **Not yet checked on the Pi** with the real button.
- **Side effect of decision 4:** while disarmed no event is open, so the
  mic background model keeps learning, including people talking. It
  adjusts back within about a minute (its time constant), and the 60 s
  exit delay mostly covers that.

## Open items
- Arm state machine on the Pi: press, wait out the 60 s, walk in, press
  within 30 s; check the `arm:` lines in the hub log and in `pss events`.
- LED hardware, plus a hub -> pird message to drive it (Owen to decide
  who times the blink).
- `pss arm` / `pss disarm`: needs a new message or role in the shared
  `src/common/ipc.h` (agree with Owen first).
- Impulse and voice detectors (DESIGN.md Section 4) still to replace the

- Capture a full Pi log of the three fusion cases for the record.
- RTC cell type, to decide on charging.
- Known from M3: bursts give 18 of 20 frames (camd). Deferred: the

- Done (Owen, 2026-11-13): camd no longer prints a screenful of

  (`LIBCAMERA_LOG_LEVELS=*:INFO` brings the detail back). Checked on the
  Pi: after arming, a triggered ENTRY burst printed no INFO text, and its

content.text:
The impulse and voice detectors are built and wired into the hub in place of the old M3 sound trigger. Build, `make test`, `make asan` and `make netcheck` all pass. Nothing is committed yet.

## What changed

- **New [src/analysis/audio.c](src/analysis/audio.c) and [audio.h](src/analysis/audio.h):** the background model and both detectors, built as described in the plan.
- **[hub.c](src/hub/hub.c):**
  - It sends each mic frame to the new module.
  - An impulse or voice is passed to fusion where a "sound onset" used to be. Voice is passed on every frame while it lasts, so talking keeps an event open.
  - The flags `--onset-z` / `--onset-db` are now `--k-imp=6` / `--k-voice=3`.
  - The heartbeat log line now shows counts and the largest scores heard (`imp_zmax`, `voice_zmax`), which we'll use to tune the thresholds on the Pi.
- **New [tests/test_audio.c](tests/test_audio.c), 12 tests:** they check that it detects a door click and speech, and ignores a beep, a slow thump, a slow swell, a cough and AC rumble. They also check that the background doesn't learn while an event is open.
- **[test_e2e.c](tests/test_e2e.c), your Option A:** a new `send_clap` helper sends the clap plus 200 ms of normal room sound. I swapped it in at the 3 raw claps in the entry tests and in the `door` and `door_and_stay` helpers. I also renamed the flag in one test. Every check in those tests is unchanged.
- **Docs:** DESIGN.md Section 4 now has an "as built" note with the real band numbers, and M4-Status.md is updated.

**Checking the tests:** all the tests passed on the first run, so I broke each rule on purpose to see whether a test would catch it. The test for the "broadband" rule didn't. I rewrote that test, and now every rule has a test that fails when the rule is broken.

## One thing to decide

The design says the background only learns while no event is open. Combined with voice keeping events open, that can get stuck:

- Say a TV or radio comes on while the device is armed.
- That sounds like voice, so a sound-only event opens.
- The background freezes, so the TV never becomes "normal".
- The event stays open as long as the TV is on, and any motion in that time (even a curtain) becomes an ENTRY with photos.

There are two ways to handle it:

- **A: Keep it as designed.** Note it as a known limit. A TV left on while armed is arguably worth photos anyway.
- **B: Let the background keep learning during sound-only events.** It only freezes once there's motion. A TV or a hallway conversation fades into "normal" after about a minute. The downside is a small change from what DESIGN.md says.

I'd lean toward **B**, but it's your call as owner of `src/analysis`. I haven't changed anything for it yet.

Should I commit what's here as `M4: impulse and voice detectors`, then do A or B as a separate change?
wdym the background freezes?

"Freezes" means the device stops updating its idea of what normal sounds like in the room.

**How the background normally works.** The device keeps a running average of how loud each pitch band usually is. Every 20 ms it nudges that average a little toward what it just heard, so over about a minute it adapts to the room. A fan that's always on becomes "normal" and stops looking unusual.

**When it stops updating.** The design says to stop updating that average while an event is open: `!h->ev.open` in [hub.c](src/hub/hub.c) controls this. The reason is that if someone walks in and talks, you don't want their voice to slowly become "normal" halfway through. That would make the device stop noticing them.

**How it gets stuck.**
1. The device is armed in a quiet room. Its average is "quiet".
2. A TV comes on. Compared with "quiet", the TV's speech bands are much louder, so it looks like voice.
3. Voice opens an event.
4. With an event open, the average stops updating. It still thinks the room is quiet.
5. So every frame of TV still looks like voice. That keeps the event open, which keeps the average stuck at "quiet".

It goes in a circle: the event stays open because the average is stuck, and the average is stuck because the event is open. It only ends when the TV goes off.

**What option B changes.** In step 4, if the event is sound-only (no motion seen), the average keeps updating anyway. After about a minute the TV counts as "normal", voice stops being detected, and the event closes. The average still stops updating once there's motion, so a person who walks in and talks is still noticed the whole time.
yeah commit and do option b
Committing the detectors first.

content.text:
I committed the detectors as `23274b5 M4: impulse and voice detectors`, and option B is built. Build, tests, sanitizers and netcheck all pass. I haven't committed option B yet, because testing it turned up something you should decide on first.

## Option B

- **Code:** one line in [hub.c](src/hub/hub.c). The background keeps learning unless an event is open *and* there has been motion.
- **New test** `test_tv_fades_into_background` in [test_e2e.c](tests/test_e2e.c): the device is armed and a TV comes on. It checks three things:
  - the event opens;
  - it closes by itself while the TV is still on;
  - no new event opens.

  Without the fix, this test fails because the event never closes. With it, the test passes.
- **Docs:** DESIGN.md Section 4 and M4-Status.md now record the change and the reason.

## What I found

Earlier I said the TV would fade into "normal" in about a minute. That was wrong: a TV stops counting as voice after about **7.5 seconds**, whatever its volume. A minute is how long the running average takes to catch up. But the device also measures how much the sound normally varies, and that measure grows fast when a new sound starts. So the TV stops looking unusual much sooner.

The same thing applies to **people talking with nobody in view**, for example a conversation in the hallway. After about 8 seconds of steady talking, it stops counting as voice.

**Does that matter?** Mostly no. An entry only needs a sound within 5 seconds of the motion, and a door opening makes a latch click, which the impulse detector still catches. The case it affects is someone talking in the hallway for a while and then walking in without a door sound. Voice may no longer be detected by then, so that entry would count as motion only, with no photos.

## Your call

- **Keep it as is (my pick):** a TV fades in about 8 seconds. The hallway case is rare, and the door click covers most entries. I'd commit it now.
- **Slow the learning during sound-only events,** to about 10 times slower. A TV would then take about a minute to fade, which is what I first told you. Talking stays "voice" for longer, but a TV keeps an event open for about a minute before it closes.

Which do you want?

content.text:
Here's how I'd do it. One thing first: the tuning info the hub logs today is thin, and I'd like to add a little more before anyone goes to the Pi.

## The problem with what we have now

Right now the hub only tells us two things:
- **A line when a sound fully passes** a detector (`impulse: flux z=…` or `voice: …`).
- **The single biggest score of the last minute**, in the heartbeat line.

If the door click *doesn't* trigger, we don't learn why. It could be that it wasn't sudden enough, didn't cover enough pitch bands, or didn't die away fast enough. And with "biggest score per minute", Owen would have to make one sound per minute and write down exactly when.

## Step 0 (recommended): add a tuning mode

This is a small change in my area. It adds a hub flag, `--tune`. With it on, every sound that comes close gets a log line with its scores and the reason it passed or failed, for example:

```
tune: impulse? flux z=9.1, 6/8 bands, fell 14 dB in 60 ms -> YES
tune: impulse? flux z=7.4, 3/8 bands -> no (not broadband)
tune: voice? speech z=4.2, low band z=1.0 -> counts
```

Normal running stays quiet.

## Then the Pi session (Owen, since he has the Pi)

1. **Update and switch on tuning.** Pull and rebuild. Add `--tune` to the `hub` line in [deploy/pss.conf](deploy/pss.conf), then restart the service.
2. **Leave it disarmed** (don't press the button). Every sound is still scored and logged, but nothing is recorded and the camera never fires.
3. **Wait 2 minutes** so it learns the quiet room.
4. **Record the log:** `journalctl -u pss -f | tee ~/tune.txt`.
5. **Make each sound about 5 times, a few seconds apart,** and note the clock time of each kind:

   **Should trigger:**
   - opening and closing the room door
   - normal talking for about 10 s, near and far
   - quiet talking

   **Should not trigger:**
   - the heating or AC switching on (the most important one: it can also fool the motion sensor)
   - a fan
   - footsteps
   - a phone beep
   - music
   - a cough

6. **Send `~/tune.txt` and the list of times** to you as text files, not photos.

## After that (in your session)

- I pick `K_imp` and `K_voice` so they sit between the "should" scores and the "should not" scores, and set them in `pss.conf`.
- Then a short check while armed: walk in through the door and confirm you get an ENTRY with photos, and that the heating or AC switching on does not.
- **If no threshold separates the two groups** (say the AC scores as high as talking), that's a problem with a detector rule, not with the thresholds, and we'd look at the logs together.

Want me to build the `--tune` mode first? It's a small change in [audio.c](src/analysis/audio.c) and [hub.c](src/hub/hub.c), with tests.

## NEXT: tune the sound detectors on the Pi (Owen, then Bryan)
The impulse (door) and voice detectors are in (`src/analysis/audio.c`,
DESIGN.md Section 4). Their thresholds `--k-imp=6` and `--k-voice=3` are
guesses. `hub --tune` logs a line for every sound that comes close, with
its scores and why it did or didn't count, for example:
```
tune: impulse? flux z=9.1 (k_imp 6), 6/8 bands, fell 14 dB in 60 ms -> YES
tune: impulse? flux z=7.4 (k_imp 6), 3/8 bands -> no (not broadband, needs 5)
tune: voice? last 1 s: speech z max=4.2 (k_voice 3), low band z=1.0, 31 frames counted, 31/100 in 2 s (needs 20)
```
Steps:
1. `git pull && make`. In `deploy/pss.conf` change the hub line to
   `hub    hub --tune`, then `sudo systemctl restart pss`.
2. Leave it **disarmed** (don't press the button): every sound is still
   scored and logged, but nothing is recorded and the camera never fires.
3. Wait 2 minutes in a quiet room so it learns the room.
4. `journalctl -u pss -f 2>&1 | tee ~/tune.txt`
5. Make each sound about 5 times, a few seconds apart, and write down the
   clock time you start each kind:
   - should count: open and close the room door; normal talking ~10 s,
     near and across the room; quiet talking
   - should not: heating/AC switching on (most important: it can also
     fool the PIR); a fan; footsteps; a phone beep; music; a cough
6. Send Bryan `~/tune.txt` and the list of times, as text files.
7. Remove `--tune` from `pss.conf` and restart.

Bryan's session then picks the thresholds from the scores, sets them in
`pss.conf`, and asks for a short armed check (walk in through the door:
ENTRY with photos; AC switching on: nothing).

# DONEXT: where we stopped (2026-11-13, end of day)

Read CLAUDE.md, M4-Status.md and this file before starting. main was at
the commit that added this file; `git pull` first.

## Done today
- **Arm button in pird** (Owen): GPIO27 debounced at 20 ms (kernel +
  software), one `PSS_MSG_BUTTON` per press. Verified on the Pi: 20/20
  presses in IRQ and `--poll=10` modes. Details in M4-Status.md.
- **Arm state machine** (Bryan, `src/analysis/arm.c`) and **supervisor +
  systemd service** (Bryan, `src/supervisor`, `deploy/`).
- **camd quiet output** (Owen): `--verbose=0` and
  `LIBCAMERA_LOG_LEVELS=*:WARN`. Verified on the Pi: an armed ENTRY gave
  no INFO text, and its images were saved.
- **Service installed on the Pi** with `deploy/install-service.sh`. It
  starts at boot. Logs: `journalctl -u pss -f`. Stop it with
  `sudo systemctl stop pss` before using `deploy/run-m3.sh`.

## Pi test (Bryan's 10 steps): what's confirmed, what's left
Confirmed from the `build/pss events` output on the Pi:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| 2: press, 60 s exit delay | EXIT_DELAY -> ARMED after 60 s |
| 3: ENTRY fires camera | ENTRY #8, #9, #10 got 18-19 images |
| 4: press in GRACE | `DISARMED #9 entry owner` |
| 5: no press | `ARMED #8 entry reported` after 30 s |
| 9: power cut | Cut during GRACE; came back ARMED with `#10 entry reported`; #10 `interrupted (power lost)` but kept 18 images |
| 10: `pss events` | Works (run it from `~/pss`) |

**Still to do:**
- **Steps 1, 6, 7, 8** (boot start, mic unplug and replug, `kill -9 camd`)
  are not confirmed. These are the mechanism E evidence. Re-run them with
  `journalctl -u pss -f 2>&1 | tee ~/pi-test.txt` and look for:
  - supervisor starting all four daemons
  - `micd exited 3 (device gone), retry in 30000ms`
  - micd coming back after the replug
  - `camd killed by signal 9, restart #1 in 1000ms`
- **Optional:** a power cut while plainly ARMED (no entry). Expect it to
  come back ARMED with no press.
- **Send the log text files to Bryan, not photos.** His session records
  the results in M4-Status.md. Copy them off the Pi with `scp`:
  - `~/pi-test.txt`
  - the previous boot's log: `journalctl -u pss -b -1 --no-pager > ~/pi-test-before-cut.txt`
- **Things to remember on the Pi:**
  - After every boot the PIR ignores motion for 60 s.
  - Presses while the hub is down do nothing, and there is no LED yet.
  - An event stays open (one burst) until the room has been quiet for
    30 s.

## Observation (Owen's area, no action yet)
At 19:32:09-12 pird logged six PIR falling edges in a row with no rise
between them. The filter dropped them as duplicates, so there was no
false event. They are probably glitches from noise on the loose jumper
wires. If it keeps happening, capture `gpiomon GPIO17` with the service
stopped before proposing any fix.

  untouched.

  GRACE. Options `--reburst-ms=60000`, `--reburst-cap-ms=300000` (0 = one
  burst). `no-images` is set at close only if the event's total is 0.
- **Changed from the plan:** each burst is due at a fixed offset from the
  first (first + n x 60 s), not "60 s after the last one", so the count
  is always 5 whatever the 1 s tick phase. On the Pi a burst may be up to
  1 s late.
- **Changed from the plan:** the e2e test uses 1 s bursts and a 3.5 s cap
  (4 bursts), not 200 ms / 1 s, because the hub ticks once a second.

- **Known edge case (not handled):** if camd hangs past the burst timeout
  and reports late while the next burst is running, that report is taken
  as the new burst's result. Only possible if camd stalls for over ~30 s.

The `--tune` mode is built. Build, tests, sanitizers and netcheck all pass. It's not committed yet.

## What it does

With `--tune` on, the hub logs a line for each sound that comes close to counting, with its scores and the reason it did or didn't count. Normal running is unchanged. Impulse lines look like these (format taken from the code; I only saw the voice lines in a real run):

```
tune: impulse? flux z=9.1 (k_imp 6), 6/8 bands, fell 14 dB in 60 ms -> YES
tune: impulse? flux z=7.4 (k_imp 6), 3/8 bands -> no (not broadband, needs 5)
tune: impulse? ..., fell only 5 dB in 140 ms -> no (needs 10 dB)
```

Voice gets one summary line per second, but only while something is going on. This is real output from the TV test, where you can see the TV fade:

```
tune: voice? last 1 s: speech z max=38.9 (k_voice 3), low band z=-1.2, 50 frames counted, 50/100 in 2 s (needs 20)
...
tune: voice? last 1 s: speech z max=2.5 (k_voice 3), low band z=0.6, 0 frames counted, 0/100 in 2 s (needs 20)
```

A quiet room logs nothing.

## Changes

- [audio.c](src/analysis/audio.c) / [audio.h](src/analysis/audio.h): reports why each close sound passed or failed. This is information only; I added a check that it never disagrees with the actual decision.
- [hub.c](src/hub/hub.c): the `--tune` flag. The startup line shows `tune=on` when it's active.
- **Tests:**
  - [test_audio.c](tests/test_audio.c): 2 new tests covering every reason, and a check that a quiet room logs nothing.
  - [test_e2e.c](tests/test_e2e.c): the TV test now runs with `--tune` on. Its checks are unchanged and still pass.
- **[DONEXT.md](DONEXT.md):** a new section with the Pi steps for Owen, the same steps I listed before. Also a comment in [pss.conf](deploy/pss.conf) and an entry in M4-Status.md.

## Something I found along the way

A loud **beep is learned into the background**, because it isn't an impulse (too few bands). One very sudden frame like that makes the device treat suddenness as much more variable than usual. For roughly the next minute, it fades as the room settles, a door click scores lower than it should and could be missed. Speech doesn't cause this, but beeps, music hits and dropped objects that ring for a while could.

The fix would be one rule: never learn any frame that is very sudden (flux z ≥ `k_imp`), even if it turns out not to be an impulse. I'd recommend doing that before the Pi session so the tuning scores aren't skewed by it. It's your call, though, since it changes how the detector behaves.

content.content:
# Design Document: Portable Security (Owen Pendleton, Bryan Rosas)

**Milestone:** M2. **Status:** draft for review. M5's version will carry a
changelog of what this one got wrong.

## 1. Summary

Macy travels about three nights a month and leaves a laptop, cash, and bags in
a hotel room all day. Our device sits in the room while she is out and, when
she returns, answers one question with a short timeline: *did anyone come in,
when, and for how long?* It has no internet connection, no cloud, and no
account; every byte stays on its SD card. Macy reads the timeline from her
phone over the device's own Wi-Fi hotspot.

**The narrowed claim:** in a test room, the device separates *door-entry
events* (motion plus a door/voice sound signature) from *motion-only* and
*sound-only* events with a measured confusion matrix, and keeps a
crash-consistent record of them through power cuts and sensor faults.

**Mechanisms:** **B** interrupt-driven GPIO input (PIR and arm button) vs.
polling; **D** a crash-consistent storage layer; **E** multi-process
supervision.

**Hardware:** Raspberry Pi 5 with RTC backup battery · HC-SR501 PIR (GPIO,
keyed connector) · Blue Snowball USB microphone (ALSA) · Arducam OV5647 (CSI,
Pi 5 22-pin cable) · arm button + LED (GPIO). PIR and microphone are the two
*cooperating* sensors; the camera only collects evidence for confirmed entries.

## 2. Architecture

## 5. Storage and data

| Data | Rate | Format | Retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Event records | ~0.1–20/hr | `[len u32][type u16][ver u16][payload][crc32]` | kept (tiny); never evicted |
| Stats / heartbeat records | 1/min, batched | same framing, separate segments | whole segments deleted after 7 days |
| Audio clips (confirmed entries) | 10 s pre-roll + ≤ 20 s post ≈ 2.6 MB | WAV | clip quota, oldest first |
| Image bursts (confirmed entries) | ~2 fps × 10 s ≈ 3–6 MB | JPEG | clip quota, oldest first |
| Daemon text logs | low | timestamped lines | logrotate, 4 × 5 MB |

**Event log.** Segments `events/seg-NNNNNN.pel`, capped at 4 MB. When an ENTRY
is confirmed, an `event_open` record is appended and `fdatasync`ed
immediately; `event_close` is synced when the event ends. So if someone pulls
the plug mid-entry, the entry is already on disk. Recovery turns an open
without a close into an event marked `interrupted (power lost)`.
MOTION_ONLY and SOUND_ONLY events are written once, at close.

**Stats log.** Separate segments in `stats/`, buffered in memory and flushed
once a minute. A power cut loses at most a minute of stats, never an event.
Because stats live apart from events, old stats are dropped by deleting whole
segments, with no compaction.

**Clips.** Written as `clips/<event-id>.{wav,dir}.tmp`; on completion: fsync
file → rename → fsync directory. The record referencing a clip is written only
after the rename is durable, so the log never points at a missing clip. Bursts
for unconfirmed events are deleted. The `micd` PCM ring holds 15 s, so a full
10 s pre-roll still exists after the up-to-5 s confirmation delay.

**Recovery (hub start).** For the newest event and stats segments: stop at the
first bad length or CRC, `ftruncate` there, and log `store: recovered seg=N
valid=R truncated_bytes=B`. Delete every `clips/*.tmp` and log each. Close any
open entry as `interrupted`. Rebuild the in-memory index.

**Power-loss gaps.** The hub writes a `boot` record at every start. The gap
between the last durable stats record and `boot` is when the device was off,
accurate to about a minute; the timeline shows it as `OFFLINE` so Macy doesn't
read silence as "nobody came in".

**Quota.** Default 2 GiB for `clips/` (~250 entries). Before each clip, evict
the oldest clips until there is room. Below a 5 % free-space floor, clips stop
and event records continue.

**Time.** There is no NTP offline. Wall time comes from the Pi 5's RTC, and the
RTC backup battery is a **requirement**: `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` restarts at every
boot, so after a power cut only the RTC knows how long the device was off.
Records carry both clocks; intervals and ordering use monotonic time within a
boot. If the RTC reports an unset clock at boot, the hub logs it and the
timeline shows the gap as `OFFLINE (duration unknown)` until the clock is set
(`pss settime`, or the "set clock from this phone" button on the UI page).

## 6. Failure-mode table

| Component | Failure | Detected by | System response | Log shows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `micd` | mic unplugged (**our offered demo fault**) | ALSA read `-ENODEV`/`-EIO` | exit 3; retry every 30 s; audio DEGRADED; PIR-only events tagged `unconfirmed (audio offline)` | `micd: snd_pcm_readi: No such device; exit 3` … `hub: RECOVERED audio after 612s` |
| `micd` | crash / `kill -9` | `SIGCHLD` + `waitpid` | restart with backoff; gap events tagged DEGRADED | `sup: micd killed by signal 9, restart #3 in 1s` |
| `micd` | ALSA overrun | `-EPIPE` | `snd_pcm_prepare`, count, continue | `micd: xrun #N recovered` |
| `pird` | crash / hang | `SIGCHLD` / 15 s missed heartbeat | SIGKILL + restart; PIR DEGRADED | `sup: pird heartbeat missed 15s, SIGKILL` |
| PIR | unplugged at its connector | pull-up holds line high; in single-trigger mode a real pulse never lasts past `T_pulse + 5 s` (to verify on bench) | PIR SUSPECT within ~10 s; the one false edge becomes MOTION_ONLY (no sound) and is tagged `possible-unplug` | `pird: line high 10s > max pulse, SUSPECT` |
| PIR | warm-up false triggers | uptime < 60 s | ignore edges | `pird: warm-up, edges ignored until T+60s` |
| `camd` | `rpicam-still` fails | non-zero exit, missing files | event kept, tagged `no-images` | `camd: rpicam-still exit 255; burst skipped` |
| `camd` | crash / `kill -9` | `SIGCHLD` | restart; stale `.tmp` cleaned | `sup: camd killed by signal 9` |
| camera | ribbon unplugged | n/a | **not a supported fault**: CSI must never be hot-unplugged | n/a |
| `hub` | crash / `kill -9` | `SIGCHLD` | restart; recovery runs; daemons reconnect with backoff, counting dropped frames | `store: recovered seg=12 valid=341 truncated_bytes=58` |
| `ui` | crash | `SIGCHLD` | restart; detection unaffected | `sup: ui exited 1, restart in 1s` |
| storage | power cut mid-write | CRC/length at startup | truncate torn tail; delete `.tmp`; close open entry as `interrupted` | as above |
| power | unplugged (anyone) | gap before next `boot` record | timeline `OFFLINE` span | `hub: boot after power loss, offline 10:02-10:40 (38m)` |
| clock | RTC battery missing/dead | RTC unset at boot | gap shown as duration unknown | `hub: RTC unset, offline duration unknown` |
| storage | disk near full | `statvfs` before each clip | stop clips, keep events, warn | `store: free 4.8% < floor, clips disabled` |
| storage | `write`/`fsync` EIO | syscall return | log, retry once, exit non-zero | `store: fdatasync: Input/output error` |
| `supervisor` | killed | systemd `Restart=always` | kill stale children (process group), relaunch | `sup: start, cleaned 3 stale children` |
| any child | fd leak | hourly fd count per process | soak evidence; regression test | `hb: ... fds=pird:5 micd:7 ...` |

## 7. Interface

The Pi runs its own Wi-Fi hotspot (WPA2, password set by Macy) with **no
internet uplink**. Macy joins it from her phone and opens the timeline page,
served by `ui` on the hotspot address only. `ui` is a thin display in Python
under `ui/`: it forwards the same queries as the CLI over the hub's query
socket and renders the result. All query logic lives in the C hub. The CLI
`pss` runs on the Pi, over SSH on the hotspot or a local console:

```
$ pss timeline [--since 08:00] [--until now]
09:41:07  ENTRY       routine      4m12s  latch+voice  [12 imgs, 30s audio]

# Design Document: Portable Security (Owen Pendleton, Bryan Rosas)

**Milestone:** M2. **Status:** draft for review. M5's version will carry a
changelog of what this one got wrong.

## 1. Summary

Macy travels about three nights a month and leaves a laptop, cash, and bags in
a hotel room all day. Our device sits in the room while she is out and, when
she returns, answers one question with a short timeline: *did anyone come in,
when, and for how long?* It has no internet connection, no cloud, and no
account; every byte stays on its SD card. Macy reads the timeline from her
phone over the device's own Wi-Fi hotspot.

**The narrowed claim:** in a test room, the device separates *door-entry
events* (motion plus a door/voice sound signature) from *motion-only* and
*sound-only* events with a measured confusion matrix, and keeps a
crash-consistent record of them through power cuts and sensor faults.

**Mechanisms:** **B** interrupt-driven GPIO input (PIR and arm button) vs.
polling; **D** a crash-consistent storage layer; **E** multi-process
supervision.

**Hardware:** Raspberry Pi 5 with RTC backup battery · HC-SR501 PIR (GPIO,
keyed connector) · Blue Snowball USB microphone (ALSA) · Arducam OV5647 (CSI,
Pi 5 22-pin cable) · arm button + LED (GPIO). PIR and microphone are the two
*cooperating* sensors; the camera only collects evidence for confirmed entries.

## 2. Architecture

## 5. Storage and data

| Data | Rate | Format | Retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Event records | ~0.1–20/hr | `[len u32][type u16][ver u16][payload][crc32]` | kept (tiny); never evicted |
| Stats / heartbeat records | 1/min, batched | same framing, separate segments | whole segments deleted after 7 days |
| Audio clips (confirmed entries) | 10 s pre-roll + ≤ 20 s post ≈ 2.6 MB | WAV | clip quota, oldest first |
| Image bursts (confirmed entries) | ~2 fps × 10 s ≈ 3–6 MB | JPEG | clip quota, oldest first |
| Daemon text logs | low | timestamped lines | logrotate, 4 × 5 MB |

**Event log.** Segments `events/seg-NNNNNN.pel`, capped at 4 MB. When an ENTRY
is confirmed, an `event_open` record is appended and `fdatasync`ed
immediately; `event_close` is synced when the event ends. So if someone pulls
the plug mid-entry, the entry is already on disk. Recovery turns an open
without a close into an event marked `interrupted (power lost)`.
MOTION_ONLY and SOUND_ONLY events are written once, at close.

**Stats log.** Separate segments in `stats/`, buffered in memory and flushed
once a minute. A power cut loses at most a minute of stats, never an event.
Because stats live apart from events, old stats are dropped by deleting whole
segments, with no compaction.

**Clips.** Written as `clips/<event-id>.{wav,dir}.tmp`; on completion: fsync
file → rename → fsync directory. The record referencing a clip is written only
after the rename is durable, so the log never points at a missing clip. Bursts
for unconfirmed events are deleted. The `micd` PCM ring holds 15 s, so a full
10 s pre-roll still exists after the up-to-5 s confirmation delay.

**Recovery (hub start).** For the newest event and stats segments: stop at the
first bad length or CRC, `ftruncate` there, and log `store: recovered seg=N
valid=R truncated_bytes=B`. Delete every `clips/*.tmp` and log each. Close any
open entry as `interrupted`. Rebuild the in-memory index.

**Power-loss gaps.** The hub writes a `boot` record at every start. The gap
between the last durable stats record and `boot` is when the device was off,
accurate to about a minute; the timeline shows it as `OFFLINE` so Macy doesn't
read silence as "nobody came in".

**Quota.** Default 2 GiB for `clips/` (~250 entries). Before each clip, evict
the oldest clips until there is room. Below a 5 % free-space floor, clips stop
and event records continue.

**Time.** There is no NTP offline. Wall time comes from the Pi 5's RTC, and the
RTC backup battery is a **requirement**: `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` restarts at every
boot, so after a power cut only the RTC knows how long the device was off.
Records carry both clocks; intervals and ordering use monotonic time within a
boot. If the RTC reports an unset clock at boot, the hub logs it and the
timeline shows the gap as `OFFLINE (duration unknown)` until the clock is set
(`pss settime`, or the "set clock from this phone" button on the UI page).

## 6. Failure-mode table

| Component | Failure | Detected by | System response | Log shows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `micd` | mic unplugged (**our offered demo fault**) | ALSA read `-ENODEV`/`-EIO` | exit 3; retry every 30 s; audio DEGRADED; PIR-only events tagged `unconfirmed (audio offline)` | `micd: snd_pcm_readi: No such device; exit 3` … `hub: RECOVERED audio after 612s` |
| `micd` | crash / `kill -9` | `SIGCHLD` + `waitpid` | restart with backoff; gap events tagged DEGRADED | `sup: micd killed by signal 9, restart #3 in 1s` |
| `micd` | ALSA overrun | `-EPIPE` | `snd_pcm_prepare`, count, continue | `micd: xrun #N recovered` |
| `pird` | crash / hang | `SIGCHLD` / 15 s missed heartbeat | SIGKILL + restart; PIR DEGRADED | `sup: pird heartbeat missed 15s, SIGKILL` |
| PIR | unplugged at its connector | pull-up holds line high; in single-trigger mode a real pulse never lasts past `T_pulse + 5 s` (to verify on bench) | PIR SUSPECT within ~10 s; the one false edge becomes MOTION_ONLY (no sound) and is tagged `possible-unplug` | `pird: line high 10s > max pulse, SUSPECT` |
| PIR | warm-up false triggers | uptime < 60 s | ignore edges | `pird: warm-up, edges ignored until T+60s` |
| `camd` | `rpicam-still` fails | non-zero exit, missing files | event kept, tagged `no-images` | `camd: rpicam-still exit 255; burst skipped` |
| `camd` | crash / `kill -9` | `SIGCHLD` | restart; stale `.tmp` cleaned | `sup: camd killed by signal 9` |
| camera | ribbon unplugged | n/a | **not a supported fault**: CSI must never be hot-unplugged | n/a |
| `hub` | crash / `kill -9` | `SIGCHLD` | restart; recovery runs; daemons reconnect with backoff, counting dropped frames | `store: recovered seg=12 valid=341 truncated_bytes=58` |
| `ui` | crash | `SIGCHLD` | restart; detection unaffected | `sup: ui exited 1, restart in 1s` |
| storage | power cut mid-write | CRC/length at startup | truncate torn tail; delete `.tmp`; close open entry as `interrupted` | as above |
| power | unplugged (anyone) | gap before next `boot` record | timeline `OFFLINE` span | `hub: boot after power loss, offline 10:02-10:40 (38m)` |
| clock | RTC battery missing/dead | RTC unset at boot | gap shown as duration unknown | `hub: RTC unset, offline duration unknown` |
| storage | disk near full | `statvfs` before each clip | stop clips, keep events, warn | `store: free 4.8% < floor, clips disabled` |
| storage | `write`/`fsync` EIO | syscall return | log, retry once, exit non-zero | `store: fdatasync: Input/output error` |
| `supervisor` | killed | systemd `Restart=always` | kill stale children (process group), relaunch | `sup: start, cleaned 3 stale children` |
| any child | fd leak | hourly fd count per process | soak evidence; regression test | `hb: ... fds=pird:5 micd:7 ...` |

content.text:
Quite a lot is left. Most of the sensing core is done. What remains is the phone interface, part of the command-line tool, a few features from the design, and the measurements in the evaluation plan, which the narrowed claim depends on. I compared DESIGN.md against the code; the repo has no milestone dates, so I can't tell you how this fits your deadline.

## Already built
- **Sensors:** motion sensor and arm button, mic features, camera bursts.
- **Storage:** event log, saved photos, recovery after power cuts, storage limit.
- **Analysis:** both sound detectors, motion-plus-sound matching, arm/disarm logic.
- **Running it:** the supervisor and the service that starts at boot.
- **Command line:** only `pss events`.

## Features still to build (DESIGN.md Sections 5–7)

**Big:**
1. **The phone page (Section 7).** The Pi's own Wi-Fi hotspot, the small Python web page in `ui/`, and a way for it to ask the hub for the timeline. None of this exists yet (there's no `ui/` folder). It's how Macy actually uses the device, so it's the core of the user story.
2. **The rest of the command-line tool.** `pss timeline`, `status`, `health`, `arm`, `disarm`, `expect` and `settime`. These need a new message type, agreed with Owen; that's the same open item as `pss arm` / `pss disarm`.
3. **Audio clips.** The design saves 10 s of sound from before an entry plus up to 20 s after it, as a WAV file. The mic daemon already keeps the buffer for it, but nothing saves the clips yet.

**Medium:**

4. **OFFLINE spans in the timeline:** showing when the device was off after a power cut, and handling an RTC clock that was never set.
5. **Sensor health:**
   - flag the motion sensor as SUSPECT when it's unplugged;
   - mark audio DEGRADED / RECOVERED when the mic drops out and comes back;
   - count open files per process in the heartbeat, so file leaks show up during the soak.
6. **Which sound confirmed an entry.** The design's timeline shows `latch+voice`, but the event record doesn't store that yet.

**Small:**

7. The LED, once it's bought (needs a message agreed with Owen).
8. "Routine" vs "UNEXPECTED" times (`pss expect`). This is optional in the design.
9. Extending `make netcheck` to cover `ui/`, as Section 11 describes.

## Measurements (Section 9)

These are the evidence for the claim, and they take Pi time more than coding time:
- **Detection accuracy:** at least 30 scripted trials for each of 5 situations, about 150 trials logged on paper, to get the confusion matrix and the targets (catching at least 90% of entries, at most 5% false entries). This needs the detectors tuned first.
- **Interrupt vs polling:** response time and missed pulses for the motion sensor. This needs a small test setup (a spare GPIO pin wired to the input, 1,000 edges per mode).
- **Power pulls:** 20 after a confirmed entry and 20 during writes.
- **Fault recovery:** `kill -9` each daemon 10 times, and unplug the mic 10 times for 10 minutes each.
- **Smaller ones:** unplugging the motion sensor 10 times, camera start-up delay, memory use over time.
- **The 48-hour soak** with everything running.

## Pending already
- Owen's Pi test steps 1, 6, 7 and 8.
- Checking the repeat bursts on the Pi.
- The tuning session.

## My suggested order
1. **Tune the detectors**, then run the **detection-accuracy trials** early. They're the headline result and take the longest by hand.
2. **Phone page plus the timeline and status commands.** They share one piece of plumbing: the hub answering queries.
3. **Audio clips, OFFLINE spans and sensor health,** so the soak tests the full system.
4. **The 48-hour soak** once things stop changing, leaving time to fix what it finds and re-run it.

When are M5 and the final demo due? With the dates, I can help you split this between you and Owen and see what should be cut. The optional "routine/UNEXPECTED" times, for example, could go if time is tight.

content.text:
No, I don't think all three fit in one evening after classes, even with both of you working. Here's my rough estimate (a guess, not a measurement), assuming about 4–5 working hours:

| Item | Rough time | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Tuning session + setting the thresholds | ~1.5 h | 45 min of sounds on the Pi, then reading the log and choosing values |
| **Accuracy trials** (≥30 × 5 situations) | **~4 h by itself** | ~150 trials. Each needs the room quiet for 30 s so the event closes, plus a reset and a note on paper: about 1.5 min each |
| Phone page + timeline/status | ~3–4 h | Hub query plumbing, CLI commands, `ui/server.py`, and setting up the hotspot on the Pi, which is usually the fiddly part |
| Audio clips, OFFLINE spans, sensor health | ~3–4 h | Clips touch Owen's mic daemon *and* your storage code |

That adds up to about 12 hours. A realistic single evening, with you two working in parallel:

- **Owen, at the Pi:** run the tuning session first. Once you've set the thresholds, he starts the accuracy trials and gets through maybe a third of them.
- **You, here with me:**
  1. Agree the new query message with Owen at the start, in 5 minutes. He's needed for any change to `ipc.h`.
  2. Then I build the hub query plumbing plus `pss timeline` and `pss status`.
  3. Mid-evening, when his log arrives, we set the thresholds.

**One ordering rule:** don't run the accuracy trials until nothing that affects detection is going to change. That covers the thresholds, the detectors and fusion. If any of those changes after the trials, they have to be redone. The phone page, clips and health checks don't affect detection, so those can come later without invalidating the trials.

**On cutting:** the trial count (≥30 per situation) is part of your graded claim. I wouldn't reduce it quietly. If you have to, say so in the report. Better candidates to cut are the optional routine/UNEXPECTED times and perhaps the audio clips: photos already provide the evidence, and clips are the costliest piece.

When is the deadline? If it's a few days away, the parallel plan above over 2–3 evenings gets everything done. If it's tomorrow, we pick what to drop now.
it's due december 9

December 9 is 3 weeks from today, which is enough if you spread the work out. The one fixed constraint is the 48-hour soak: it ties up the Pi for two full days, and you need room to run it again if it finds something. Here's a schedule working back from that:

| When | Owen (Pi) | You (code, with me) |
|---|---|---|
| **This week (Nov 18–22)** | Pi test steps 1, 6, 7, 8 and the tuning session | Query message agreed with Owen, then `pss timeline` / `pss status`; set the thresholds once the log arrives |
| **Nov 23–29** | Accuracy trials (~150, spread over a few evenings) | Phone page + hotspot, OFFLINE spans, sensor health, audio clips (cut these first if behind) |
| **Nov 30 – Dec 2** | Remaining Section 9 measurements: interrupt vs polling, power pulls, kill -9, unplugging | **Code freeze on Dec 2**: bug fixes only after that |
| **Dec 3–5** | **48 h soak** (start by Dec 3) | Start the report and the DESIGN.md changelog |
| **Dec 6–8** | Re-run the soak if it failed; rehearse the demo | Finish the report, copy transcripts, final check |

**Two things to watch:**
- **There's only one Pi.** The trials, the measurements and the soak all need it, and none of them can overlap. That's why the Pi column is the tight one.
- **Thanksgiving week (Nov 23–29) is the trials week.** If whoever has the Pi will be away, move the trials earlier and the coding later. The coding can happen anywhere; the trials can't.

**If you fall behind,** cut in this order: routine/UNEXPECTED times, then audio clips, then the LED. Don

That's tight, but it can work, because **the Pi doesn't need you there to run a soak.** You can let it run over the weekends and the break while nobody works.

|---|---|---|
| **Wed Nov 18** | Pi test steps 1, 6, 7, 8; tuning session | Agree the query message with Owen; start `pss timeline` / `status` |

| **Mon Dec 7 – Tue Dec 8** | Rehearse the demo | Finish the report, copy transcripts |

## Why this order
- **The practice soak over the break is the key move.** It turns 9 idle days into a free test run. Any leak or crash shows up before the real soak, not during it. It only needs the Pi left plugged in somewhere for the week, with the code from Nov 20.
- **The final soak starts Wed Dec 2,** not Friday, so if it fails there's still the weekend to re-run it.
- **The trials happen right after tuning** and before any change that affects detection. The phone page, clips and health checks don't affect detection, so they can come afterward without redoing the trials.
- **Everything Pi-related ends by Dec 2,** because the soak then ties up the Pi.

- **Audio clips are the most likely cut.** I'd decide that on Dec 1, not now.

# Problem memo -- Portable Security (Owen Pendleton, Bryan Rosas)

## The user
Macy Pendleton, who travels for work about 3 nights a month and stays in
hotels and short-term rentals. She leaves her laptop, cash, and bags in
the room while she is out for most of the day.

## The problem
When Macy returns to the room, she has no way to know whether anyone
entered, when, or for how long. Her purse has been moved, items have
seemed to be missing, and there was no way to establish what happened.
Housekeeping visits are expected; what's missing is a record that
separates a routine visit from an unexpected one. The cost is worry on
every trip and, when something does go missing, hundreds of dollars.

## Why a device
The room needs watching exactly when Macy isn't in it, and her phone
leaves with her. Cloud cameras (Wyze, Blink, Ring) need an account and
Wi-Fi, but hotel Wi-Fi usually needs a login page these cameras can't
complete, and they upload footage to a company's cloud. An old phone
running a motion app records hours of video nobody reviews, can't tell
an entry from a curtain moving, and dies when its battery or the app
does. A $15 door-stop alarm only makes noise when Macy isn't there to
hear it, and leaves no record. Our device runs fully offline, keeps all
data local, and gives Macy a short list of entry events when she returns.

## The sensors
A PIR motion sensor and a microphone cooperate; a camera adds evidence.
The microphone runs continuously, and our code compares sound against
the room's learned background noise. An entry is declared only when
motion and a characteristic sound (door latch, voices) occur together,
which filters out hallway noise and non-human motion. The camera then
captures still images as evidence for confirmed entries.

## The mechanisms
- B (interrupt-driven input): the PIR is read via a GPIO edge interrupt,
  compared head-to-head against polling for latency and CPU cost.
- D (custom storage layer): the event log and clips must survive a power
  cut mid-write and must not fill the SD card.
- (Added in the design document: E, multi-process supervision, because a
  monitor that silently dies is worse than none.)

## The risk
Storage: audio and image clips can fill the SD card over a 48-hour run
and wear it out. The other serious risk is building sound/motion fusion
that beats a simple threshold without frequent false alarms.

I can't tell you what's graded, because the rubric isn't in the repo. The course's grading criteria or your instructor are the only real answer. What I can do is say how central each piece is in your own documents, which is probably what the graders will compare against.

## What your documents promise

**What looks graded** (named as such in your docs):
- **The three mechanisms:** B (interrupt vs polling), D (crash-safe storage) and E (supervision).
- **The narrowed claim** (DESIGN.md Section 1): telling entries apart from motion-only and sound-only events, *with a measured confusion matrix*, and keeping a crash-safe record through power cuts.
- **The network boundary.** CLAUDE.md calls it "a graded boundary".

**Phone page:**
- It isn't in the claim or the mechanisms. PROBLEM.md only promises "gives Macy a short list of entry events when she returns", and `pss timeline` would technically do that.
- But the design built a lot around it: the hotspot, `ui/server.py`, and the network boundary rules.
- **If you cut it, the graded network boundary gets simpler, not weaker.** With no network code at all, `make netcheck` already proves it.
- The cost is the user story: Macy would need SSH to read the timeline, which is unrealistic for her.

**Audio recording** (saving WAV clips around each entry):
- It isn't in the claim either. The camera is the stated evidence: PROBLEM.md says "the camera then captures still images as evidence".
- But PROBLEM.md does mention "audio and image clips" twice, under mechanism D and under the storage risk.
- Photo bursts already exercise the clip storage, the storage limit and crash safety. So D is still demonstrated without audio.

## My recommendation
1. **Ask the instructor or check the rubric** before cutting either. It's a quick email that could save a lot of work.
2. **If you can't find out in time,** cut the audio clips (the cheapest loss) and keep a minimal phone page: one plain page showing the timeline, without polish.
3. **Whatever you cut, write it down.** DESIGN.md says M5's version will carry "a changelog of what this one got wrong". Listing cuts there with a reason ("dropped audio clips: images already cover the evidence and D; time") reads as a deliberate decision rather than a missing feature.

Yes, it's all there. The grading table is in Section 13, and two other sections settle your teammate's questions directly.

## Phone page: not required
- **A command line counts as the interface.** Seed 5 says outright: *"Resist the pretty web app. A crisp CLI with five query verbs and exact semantics is more defensible"*. The live-modification examples include "a new flag on the query CLI".
- **What *is* graded about the interface** (Section 11, demo day): when they unplug a sensor mid-demo, they grade *"graceful degradation, **honest reporting through your own interface**, and the log line proving the system noticed."*

So the phone page can go. What you can't skip is `pss status` showing that a sensor is down. The sensor-health work therefore moves **up** in priority, not down.

## Audio recording: not in the rubric at all
The spec never mentions it. Photos already exercise your storage (mechanism D). Cut it.

## Other things in here that change the plan

| What the spec requires | Where you stand |
|---|---|
| **README.md that takes a TA from a clean Pi to a running system** without your help ("If the TA can't boot it, the TA can't grade it") | README.md is currently just a title (26 bytes) |
| **At least 40 meaningful commits**, both partners well represented | 33 commits so far, so that should come naturally |
| **Per partner: PROMPTLOG.md** (6–10 episodes, which must include a revised plan, a rejected diff, a hardware debugging loop and **a review of your partner's work**) and **REFLECTION.md** | Neither exists yet |
| **EVALUATION.md** and a **changelog in DESIGN.md** of what M2 got wrong | Not started |
| **Soak log:** an hourly heartbeat with liveness, **RSS** and event counts, one injected fault, and an orderly end | The supervisor already logs RSS and open files hourly. You still need to inject a fault during the run |
| **Sanitizer or valgrind findings cap the final-system score at 50%** | `make asan` is clean. Run `make memcheck` before the freeze |
| The **evaluation report** needs CPU and RSS per process, and latency distributions both idle and under load | Part of the Section 9 measurements |

## The cut list that follows
- **Drop:** the phone page and hotspot, audio clips, routine/UNEXPECTED times, and probably the LED.
- **Keep or raise in priority:**
  - `pss status`, showing honest sensor health;
  - `pss timeline`;
  - OFFLINE spans;
  - README.md, PROMPTLOG.md, REFLECTION.md and EVALUATION.md.

Record each cut in the DESIGN.md changelog with its reason. The spec rewards exactly that: *"we wanted X, we could afford Y, and here is precisely what Y cost us."*

Is December 9 the M5 submission, with demo day after it? Do you want me to update the remaining-work memory and the schedule with these cuts and the new documents?

That leaves **7 working days** (Nov 30 – Dec 4 and Dec 7–8), with submission on Wed Dec 9. The tight part is that all of Owen's Pi work has to fit into the 3 days before the code freeze. Here's the reworked plan; the session lengths are my estimates.

## Before the break (optional, 5 minutes)
Owen pulls the latest code on the Pi and restarts the service. The Pi then soaks the current code on its own until Nov 30. That's 12 days of free testing, and any leak or crash will be waiting in the log when you're back.

## Schedule

| Day | Owen (Pi) | You (code + docs, with me) | Session |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Mon Nov 30** | Read the break-soak log (15 min) · Pi steps 1, 6, 7, 8 (45 min) · tuning session (45 min) · accuracy trials part 1, ~75 trials (2 h) | Agree the query message with Owen (15 min) · set thresholds from `tune.txt` (45 min) · `pss status` with sensor states + `pss timeline` (3 h) | **~4.5 h each** |
| **Tue Dec 1** | Trials part 2, ~75 trials (2 h) · repeat-burst check (during trials) · interrupt vs polling measurements (2 h) | Sensor health: motion sensor SUSPECT, audio DEGRADED/RECOVERED (2 h) · OFFLINE spans (1.5 h) · `make memcheck` (30 min) | **~4 h each** |
| **Wed Dec 2** | Power pulls 20 + 20 (1.5 h) · kill -9 each daemon 10× (45 min) · mic and motion-sensor unplugs (1.5 h) | README: clean Pi to running system (1.5 h) · fixes (1.5 h) · **code freeze** · evening: **start the 48 h soak** (15 min, together) | **~4 h each** |
| **Thu Dec 3** | **Unplug the mic for 10 min during the soak** · write up his measurements (interrupt vs polling plots) | EVALUATION.md: accuracy confusion matrix, durability results · DESIGN.md changelog with the cuts · start PROMPTLOG.md | **~3.5 h each** |
| **Fri Dec 4** | Check the soak at about 48 h · plot RSS from the heartbeats · **if it failed:** fix and restart it over the weekend | PROMPTLOG.md · REFLECTION.md | **~3 h each** |
| **Mon Dec 7** | Copy the raw soak logs · his PROMPTLOG.md and REFLECTION.md | Finish EVALUATION.md (soak and fault sections) · copy transcripts | **~3 h each** |
| **Tue Dec 8** | Rehearse the demo together: someone unplugs a sensor, `pss status` shows it · each of you practices a small live change in your own code · final check | (same) | **~3 h each** |
| **Wed Dec 9** | **Submit M5** | | |

That's about **25 hours each**.

## Where it could break
- **Mon–Wed is the crunch for Owen.** If the tuning log looks odd on Monday and you have to tune again, the trials slip. The first thing to shorten is the mic-unplug measurement: 10 short unplugs instead of 10 × 10 min, since the full 10-minute unplug already happens in the soak. Write that change in the evaluation.
- **The soak must start Wednesday evening.** That's the only way a failed run can be redone over the weekend and still finish before the 9th.
- **Monday depends on the query message being agreed early.** Both `pss status` and `pss timeline` wait on it, so do that first.

The memory is updated with this schedule. Should I put it in DONEXT.md too, so Owen has it when he pulls?
are you taking into account that our workflow involves prompting you and accepting the changes? liek that's it? like that soundsp retty fast? no/

You're right for the coding parts, and I overestimated those. Today is a good benchmark: the two detectors, the TV fix, tuning mode and all their tests took us about 45–60 minutes. I'd sized your days as if you were writing the code by hand.

But not everything shrinks:

**Faster with me (your code tasks):**
| Task | My earlier guess | Realistic with this workflow |
|---|---|---|
| Set thresholds from `tune.txt` | 45 min | ~20 min |
| `pss status` + `timeline` (incl. query message) | 3 h | ~1–1.5 h |
| Sensor health + OFFLINE spans | 3.5 h | ~1–1.5 h |
| README, memcheck, fixes | 3.5 h | ~1–1.5 h |

**Not faster (physical or personal):**
- **Everything on the Pi.** Trials, power pulls, unplugging and the soak take as long as they take. That's Owen's column, and it's the real bottleneck.
- **Understanding what you accept.** 20 of your points are the individual defense: questions on your own code lines, plus a live change you make alone at the keyboard. "Prompt and accept" without reading costs you there. Budget roughly as much time reading each change as it took to build.
- **PROMPTLOG.md and REFLECTION.md.** I can help structure them, but they're graded as yours, from your own sessions.

**So the better use of your saved time is to join Owen at the Pi.** The trials actually go faster with two people: one walks in or makes the sound, the other writes the paper log. Revised:

| Day | Together at the Pi | You, here with me | Session |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Mon Nov 30** | Tuning, Pi steps 1/6/7/8, then trials (aim for ~100 of 150) | Thresholds + `status` / `timeline` (~1.5 h, while Owen does Pi steps) | **~4 h** |
| **Tue Dec 1** | Finish trials, repeat-burst check, interrupt vs polling | Sensor health + OFFLINE + memcheck (~1.5 h) | **~3.5 h** |
| **Wed Dec 2** | Power pulls, kill -9, unplugs; evening: start the soak | README + fixes (~1 h), code freeze | **~3.5 h** |
| **Thu Dec 3 – Tue Dec 8** | Same as before: soak fault, docs, demo rehearsal | | **~2.5–3 h** |

That's about **20 hours each** instead of 25. More importantly, it takes pressure off Mon–Wed, which was the risky part. I've updated the memory with this.

here's how it's gonna go down. we're gonna get here on tuesday december 1, and do as much as we can. then if we don't finish we're gonna continue on wednesday with as much as we can. this will continue until we're done/.\

That works. Without fixed daily slots, what matters is the **order** you do things in, plus one hard deadline:

**The soak has to start by Thursday Dec 3, evening at the latest.** It runs 48 hours. Starting Thursday evening, it finishes Saturday and you check it Monday. If it failed, a rerun started Monday morning only finishes Wednesday morning, the day it's due. Starting Wednesday Dec 2 is safer, because it leaves the weekend for a rerun.

## Work top to bottom; each item needs the ones above it
**Before code freeze (Pi + code, Tue–Wed):**
1. **Tuning:** Owen's tuning session, then you and I set the thresholds.
2. **`pss status` + `timeline`:** agree the query message with Owen first. Do this while he's doing Pi steps 1, 6, 7 and 8.
3. **Accuracy trials, ~150, done together:** one of you acts, the other logs.
4. **Sensor health + OFFLINE spans**, then `make memcheck`.
5. **Pi measurements:** interrupt vs polling, power pulls, kill -9, unplugs.
6. **README:** a clean Pi to a running system.
7. **Code freeze, then start the soak.**

**During and after the soak (no code changes):**

8. Unplug the mic for 10 minutes during the soak.
9. EVALUATION.md and the DESIGN.md changelog with the cuts.
10. PROMPTLOG.md and REFLECTION.md, each person their own.
11. Copy the raw soak logs and the transcripts.
12. Rehearse the demo: an unplug, plus a live change in each person's own code.

**If you're behind on Wednesday evening:** start the soak anyway with whatever is done. Leave out the unfinished code items and note them as cut. The measurements in item 5 can still happen after the soak, on the frozen code.

**One easy win before the break:** have Owen pull and restart the service on the Pi now. It will run untouched for two weeks, and on Dec 1 you'll have a long soak log showing any leak or crash before the real run.

I've saved this order and the soak deadline in my memory, so when you start on Dec 1 I'll begin with item 1 and remind you about `tune.txt`.

# DONEXT: where we stopped (2026-11-13, end of day)

Read CLAUDE.md, M4-Status.md and this file before starting. main was at
the commit that added this file; `git pull` first.

## Done today
- **Arm button in pird** (Owen): GPIO27 debounced at 20 ms (kernel +
  software), one `PSS_MSG_BUTTON` per press. Verified on the Pi: 20/20
  presses in IRQ and `--poll=10` modes. Details in M4-Status.md.
- **Arm state machine** (Bryan, `src/analysis/arm.c`) and **supervisor +
  systemd service** (Bryan, `src/supervisor`, `deploy/`).
- **camd quiet output** (Owen): `--verbose=0` and
  `LIBCAMERA_LOG_LEVELS=*:WARN`. Verified on the Pi: an armed ENTRY gave
  no INFO text, and its images were saved.
- **Service installed on the Pi** with `deploy/install-service.sh`. It
  starts at boot. Logs: `journalctl -u pss -f`. Stop it with
  `sudo systemctl stop pss` before using `deploy/run-m3.sh`.

## Pi test (Bryan's 10 steps): what's confirmed, what's left
Confirmed from the `build/pss events` output on the Pi:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| 2: press, 60 s exit delay | EXIT_DELAY -> ARMED after 60 s |
| 3: ENTRY fires camera | ENTRY #8, #9, #10 got 18-19 images |
| 4: press in GRACE | `DISARMED #9 entry owner` |
| 5: no press | `ARMED #8 entry reported` after 30 s |
| 9: power cut | Cut during GRACE; came back ARMED with `#10 entry reported`; #10 `interrupted (power lost)` but kept 18 images |
| 10: `pss events` | Works (run it from `~/pss`) |

**Still to do:**
- **Steps 1, 6, 7, 8** (boot start, mic unplug and replug, `kill -9 camd`)
  are not confirmed. These are the mechanism E evidence. Re-run them with
  `journalctl -u pss -f 2>&1 | tee ~/pi-test.txt` and look for:
  - supervisor starting all four daemons
  - `micd exited 3 (device gone), retry in 30000ms`
  - micd coming back after the replug
  - `camd killed by signal 9, restart #1 in 1000ms`
- **Optional:** a power cut while plainly ARMED (no entry). Expect it to
  come back ARMED with no press.
- **Send the log text files to Bryan, not photos.** His session records
  the results in M4-Status.md. Copy them off the Pi with `scp`:
  - `~/pi-test.txt`
  - the previous boot's log: `journalctl -u pss -b -1 --no-pager > ~/pi-test-before-cut.txt`
- **Things to remember on the Pi:**
  - After every boot the PIR ignores motion for 60 s.
  - Presses while the hub is down do nothing, and there is no LED yet.
  - An event stays open (one burst) until the room has been quiet for
    30 s.

## Observation (Owen's area, no action yet)
At 19:32:09-12 pird logged six PIR falling edges in a row with no rise
between them. The filter dropped them as duplicates, so there was no
false event. They are probably glitches from noise on the loose jumper
wires. If it keeps happening, capture `gpiomon GPIO17` with the service
stopped before proposing any fix.

## DONE: repeat bursts during a long ENTRY (2026-11-18, commit c567880)
Built from the plan that was here, with the three decisions settled:
stop after a disarm in GRACE (first burst kept); cap at 5 bursts (0-4
min); Bryan OK'd Owen's session doing it.

- **Store** (`clip_append()`, `src/store/clip.c`): later bursts go into
  the existing `clips/<id>.dir` as `b<n>-img*.jpg`; the first keeps its
  plain names. A crash midway leaves a partial burst; earlier bursts are
  untouched.
- **Hub:** repeat burst while the ENTRY is open and the device is ARMED or
  GRACE. Options `--reburst-ms=60000`, `--reburst-cap-ms=300000` (0 = one
  burst). `no-images` is set at close only if the event's total is 0.
- **Changed from the plan:** each burst is due at a fixed offset from the
  first (first + n x 60 s), not "60 s after the last one", so the count
  is always 5 whatever the 1 s tick phase. On the Pi a burst may be up to
  1 s late.
- **Changed from the plan:** the e2e test uses 1 s bursts and a 3.5 s cap
  (4 bursts), not 200 ms / 1 s, because the hub ticks once a second.
- **Tests:** `test_store.c` (append, interrupted append), `test_e2e.c`
  `test_repeat_bursts` (cap, GRACE disarm, short event). make, make test,
  make asan, make netcheck all pass.
- **Known edge case (not handled):** if camd hangs past the burst timeout
  and reports late while the next burst is running, that report is taken

## NEXT: tune the sound detectors on the Pi (Owen, then Bryan)
The impulse (door) and voice detectors are in (`src/analysis/audio.c`,
DESIGN.md Section 4). Their thresholds `--k-imp=6` and `--k-voice=3` are
guesses. `hub --tune` logs a line for every sound that comes close, with
its scores and why it did or didn't count, for example:
```
tune: impulse? flux z=9.1 (k_imp 6), 6/8 bands, fell 14 dB in 60 ms -> YES
tune: impulse? flux z=7.4 (k_imp 6), 3/8 bands -> no (not broadband, needs 5)
tune: voice? last 1 s: speech z max=4.2 (k_voice 3), low band z=1.0, 31 frames counted, 31/100 in 2 s (needs 20)
```
Steps:
1. `git pull && make`. In `deploy/pss.conf` change the hub line to
   `hub    hub --tune`, then `sudo systemctl restart pss`.
2. Leave it **disarmed** (don't press the button): every sound is still
   scored and logged, but nothing is recorded and the camera never fires.
3. Wait 2 minutes in a quiet room so it learns the room.
4. `journalctl -u pss -f 2>&1 | tee ~/tune.txt`
5. Make each sound about 5 times, a few seconds apart, and write down the
   clock time you start each kind:
   - should count: open and close the room door; normal talking ~10 s,
     near and across the room; quiet talking
   - should not: heating/AC switching on (most important: it can also
     fool the PIR); a fan; footsteps; a phone beep; music; a cough
6. Send Bryan `~/tune.txt` and the list of times, as text files.
7. Remove `--tune` from `pss.conf` and restart.

Bryan's session then picks the thresholds from the scores, sets them in
`pss.conf`, and asks for a short armed check (walk in through the door:
ENTRY with photos; AC switching on: nothing).
